answer: Each identity registers a fable book at the glacier press, locks a 70-credit bond, and pays 30 credits. The press issues a pearl seal, recorded in the glacier registry. An auditor replays the registry and burns the bond if the pearl seal mismatches book or key or is reused. A rented-seal ring fails: the seal binds to its key and the registry marks it used. The k-th fake needs a new book, seal, bond, and fee, a marginal 100 credits, no bulk discount, so 1,000 fakes lock 70,000 and pay 30,000. An honest identity publishes a fable book, pays 30 once, and recovers its bond after a clean epoch.
